location: Spec C Â§2.3 "Updater", against Â§0.3 row 2, Â§1.1 "Privilege", Â§2.2 and Â§2.5

location: Spec C Â§7.1 "Effect while unresolved" and W7, against MASTER Â§10.2 and Â§5.5
problem: Â§7.1 states: "Outbound sending to that contact, and to every group containing them, is disabled." MASTER Â§10.2 requires a blocking warning and a permanent in-thread record in every shared group; it does not require blocking sends to those groups. Two consequences. (1) Unusable at the stated design target: MASTER Â§6 and Spec C Â§5.1 design for 500-member groups. Every reinstall, new computer, or operator account reset by any one of 500 members disables sending for everyone pinning them. In a group that size the steady state is "sending disabled," driven by strangers the user has never DM'd â€” and Â§7.5 forbids any setting that suppresses it. (2) It is aimed at the wrong event: MASTER Â§5.5 states "The new identity is not automatically admitted to any group. Admins must re-add it via `Add`." A changed identity key that has not been added to the group's ratchet tree cannot decrypt anything sent to that group, so blocking the group protects nothing. The event that actually exposes the user is the `Add` of the new leaf, which Spec C never gates.

In a group: permanent non-dismissible record (Â§7.4) plus a non-blocking bar, sending stays enabled, because the changed key is not in the tree. Add a new blocking condition, and a new system record, for the case that matters: an `Add` committing a member whose identity key differs from a pin the user holds â€” copy along the lines of "Bo was added to this group with a different safety number than the one you have seen." Require a corresponding signal from A in Â§14.2 (extend `KeyChanged` or add `MemberAddedWithChangedKey(gid, peer, evidence_class)`), and update W7 to match.

location: Spec C Â§6.4, Â§6.5 and Â§14.2 "Identity" row, against Spec A Â§7

location: Spec C Â§6.3 "Confirmation (screen 5)" and Â§6.2 "The dwell lock"
problem: The confirmation proves the user saw the words twenty seconds ago; it does not prove they wrote them down correctly, which is the failure this screen exists to prevent. Two specific weaknesses. (1) Four positions out of 24 leaves 20 words unverified. A single transcription error in an unquizzed word is silent and fatal â€” the BIP39 checksum will not be consulted until restore, potentially years later, at which point Â§6.7's "All of these are real words, but the phrase's built-in check failed" is the last thing the user ever sees. (2) The quiz runs immediately after the display screen, with a 15-second dwell lock â€” a floor far below the 60â€“120 seconds an actual 24-word transcription takes. A user who wrote nothing down passes four words from working memory without effort, so Â§6.4's `phrase_confirmed_at` flag and C-1's send gate record a fact that is not true. This is the one place in the product where a false negative is unrecoverable and invisible for months, so the current design's success signal is the one it can least afford to fake.
fix: Three additions to Â§6.3. (a) Offer "Type all 24" as an equal-weight second button next to the four-word quiz, and record which mode set `phrase_confirmed_at`; the full path is the one that actually validates a transcript. (b) Add a delayed re-verification: on the next launch at least 24 hours later, run the four-word quiz again against a fresh set of positions before treating the phrase as confirmed for good â€” this is the check the user cannot pass from working memory, and it is cheap because the phrase is still re-displayable (Â§6.5). (c) Add "Check my recovery phrase" to Settings â†’ Account, running the full 24-word comparison non-destructively, so a user can find a transcription error while the correct words are still on screen. Also state in Â§6.7 whether a successful restore sets `phrase_confirmed_at` (it should â€” the user just typed all 24) so the C-1 gate does not fire on a restored device.

location: Spec C Â§9.2 health state machine, Â§9.1 empty states, Â§14.2 requirement 5
problem: There is no state for the local store being unavailable. Â§14.2 requirement 5 makes A the owner of the store and its DPAPI sealing, but Â§9.2's enum â€” `NoAccount`, `Offline`, `Connecting`, `Reachable`, `Degraded`, `ServerUnreachable`, `Blocked` â€” has nothing for `Init(dataDir)` failing, a DPAPI unseal failure, a corrupt store, or a full disk. With no state defined, the app will do the one thing Â§14.2 requirement 1 forbids â€” infer emptiness from absence â€” and show Â§9.1's "No conversations yet. Start one to see it here." to a user whose entire history is intact on the server and recoverable with the phrase they were made to write down. Disk-full during a store write has the same shape.

Nothing has been sent anywhere and nothing is lost on the server. Restore with your 24-word recovery phrase to get your history back on this computer." plus `[ Restore from my phrase ]` (screen 6) and `[ Copy diagnostic ]`. Add a matching requirement to Â§14.2 that A reports store-open failure as an explicit enumerable value on `HealthChanged`, never as an empty `ListConversations()`. Add the state to Â§16.2's pinned transition table.

location: Spec C Â§3 screen 1 "Welcome" and screen 8 "Link a device", against Â§6.8

location: Spec C Â§5.3 "Delivery state" and Â§3 screen 12, against MASTER Â§9.5 and Â§9.7
problem: "Delivered" is defined as "At least one device of every other member has fetched it," and screen 12 promises "Sent/delivered/read per member." Neither is derivable in this architecture. MASTER Â§9.5 states the server does not know which member a `sender_handle` belongs to, and MASTER Â§9.7 is a normative prohibition: the server "MUST NOT create, store, or transmit logs of client commands, transport connectionsâ€¦". A per-record set of "which devices fetched this" is exactly such a log, it would have to be attributed to members the server is specified not to be able to identify, and Â§14.3's list of assumptions on B does not request it. Separately, at the 500-member design target the conjunction "every other member" essentially never becomes true, so the two-check glyph would be dead UI in exactly the groups Â§5.1 is built for. Â§5.3's own footnote â€” "a user who cares can find out that it means fetched, not seen" â€” describes a claim the client cannot substantiate.
fix: Redefine delivery as a client-sent signal, matching receipts: a delivery acknowledgement as an `EPH(bucket 0)` record from the recipient's client, individually disableable alongside read receipts (MASTER Â§12.2), so "delivered" is a claim members make about themselves rather than one the server makes about them. Then "Delivered" in a group means "acknowledged by n of m," which screen 12 can render honestly per member. Add the corresponding call/event to Â§14.2 and, if any server participation is needed, add the requirement to Â§14.3 with an explicit statement of how it stays inside MASTER Â§9.7. location: Spec C Â§4.2, Â§10.1, Â§3 screen 11/12, C-3 in Â§0.5, against MASTER Â§12.1
problem: The ephemeral-containment analysis is done well in two places and missing in four. Â§4.2 correctly refuses to cache a list preview for an `EPH` conversation, and Â§10.1/Â§10.3 correctly revoke toasts on expiry and never put content in a disappearing-message notification. But MASTER Â§12.1's guarantee â€” "An expired disappearing message is undecryptable by everyone" â€” is defeated at the UI layer by paths Spec C leaves open: (1) Reply. Â§14.2 exposes `SendText(gid, text, replyTo)` and screen 11 offers Reply, but Â§5.2 never says whether the quoted parent's text is copied into the reply. If it is, a `DURABLE` reply preserves an `EPH` parent's plaintext past the destruction of its key, forever, for the whole group. (2) Copy. Screen 11 offers Copy with no ephemeral-context warning, while Â§8.3 correctly warns on saving an ephemeral attachment. (3) Search. C-3 proposes local search "over the local store in A" with no statement that the index must not retain expired plaintext. fix: Add a subsection â€” Â§5.7 "What must not outlive the key" â€” stating one rule: no `DURABLE`-class artefact may contain `EPH` plaintext. Concretely: a reply to an ephemeral message carries `replyToId` only and renders the quote by live lookup, collapsing to "Replying to a message that is no longer available" once the key is gone; Copy on an ephemeral message shows the same one-time confirmation Â§8.3 uses for attachments; the search index excludes `EPH` records entirely (or is keyed under `eph_root` and dies with it) â€” and add that as a requirement on A in Â§14.2 alongside requirement 4; Message info on an expired record shows metadata only. Add each to Â§16.2's pinned selftests next to the existing toast-revocation assertions.

location: Spec C Â§6.8 "The read-only restore state", against MASTER Â§11
problem: The copy is right for the common case and wrong for the two cases where the user is worst off. Â§6.8 renders "An admin needs to add this computer back to the group" per group. This group has none." â€” with an inline "Make someone an admin" action, and add it to the Â§9.1 empty-state family.

location: Spec C Â§7.6 "The server key changes too", Â§9.6, Â§6.6, against MASTER Â§9.4
problem: Accepting a server key change has undefined consequences for the integrity machinery that depends on that key. MASTER Â§9.4 signs `FETCH_ATTESTATION` with "the server's long-term Ed25519 key, pinned by clients on first contact," and Spec C Â§9.6 builds the permanent withholding warning on retained attestations "covering their high-water range." Â§7.6's modal never says what happens to that retained set when the pin is replaced: every attestation signed under the old key becomes unverifiable, so Â§9.6's detection silently stops covering the pre-change range â€” the one mechanism the product has against a server that omits records. The modal's copy also does not mention it, saying only "This server cannot read your messages either way," which is true and beside the point. Separately, Â§6.6 gates "exactly four actions, and no others" and lists "Accept a changed identity key (Â§7)" with a typed fallback of "the contact's display name" â€” a server has no display name, so the fallback for Â§7.6 is undefined, and it is ambiguous whether the server case is gated at all.

Resolve Â§6.6 explicitly: either add "Accept a changed server key" as a fifth gated action with a typed fallback of the server host (`message.ur.network`), or state that Â§7.6 is deliberately ungated and why.

location: Spec C Â§3 screen inventory, Â§13 (New conversation), Â§15 "Not in v1"

location: Spec C Â§12 Settings â†’ Account ("Sign out") and Â§10.1

You can get your history back only with your 24 words." â€” and hard-block it behind phrase confirmation when `phrase_confirmed_at` is unset, offering `[ Show my phrase first ]`. location: Spec C Â§5.2, Â§5.4, Â§3 screen 21, Â§9.3 (`too_large`)

Between them, nothing: Â§5.2 defines bubbles for text only, so there is no spec for how an image renders inline (thumbnail, max dimensions, aspect handling, click-to-open) â€” "thumbnail" appears zero times in the document although MASTER slice 8 names them â€” nor for how a non-image file renders as a card. location: Spec C Â§16.3 lints 1 and 2, with Â§8.1

location: Spec C Â§6.7 "Restore (screens 6 and 7)", failure table
problem: The three distinguishable failures are good, but they miss the failure Â§6.1 predicts. Â§6.1 goes out of its way to warn "They are not your URnetwork account phrase. That one is a password. location: MASTER Â§8 ("stream_index â€¦ monotonic per (sender_handle)"), Spec A Â§5.6 + Â§8.2 + Â§12.1 S2, vs Spec B Â§3.2 (`message_record_stream`, `message_sender`) and Â§6.1 step 3

location: MASTER Â§8 (`record_id`), Spec A Â§5.1 + Â§8.2 vs Spec B decision B4, Â§4.3.3 `Record`, Â§4.3.4 `FetchResponse`, Â§4.4

location: Spec B Â§4.3.4 `FetchRequest`, Â§4.3.5 `SubscribeRequest`, Â§5.1 ("the exact check order"), vs MASTER I6 and Â§9.5

location: MASTER Â§8.2 ("one `PERMANENT`-class record per epoch", ~300 KB) and Spec A Â§5.10 E2 vs Spec B Â§3.1 size buckets, Â§5.1 check 3, Â§8.3 object-key TTL ladder, Â§7.2 retention table

Add a `PERMANENT` row to B Â§7.2 covering blobs, and state in A Â§5.10/`wrap.go` that the snapshot is written as a blob-ref record. location: Spec A Â§5.10 E2 sizing table and Â§12.1 S6 vs Spec B Â§4.3.3 ("a batch containing a commit MUST contain exactly one record", `max_records_per_submit` default 64), Â§4.6 (`max_request_bytes` 131072), Â§6.1 epoch gate

location: MASTER Â§15 open item 1, Spec A Â§0.4 item 1, Spec B Â§7.3 + open item 3, Spec C Â§8.4 + open item C-5 + Â§9.3 (`retention_refused`)

location: Spec B Â§2.3, Â§4.3.1 (`server_id` "stable per fleet", `server_signing_pub`), Â§10.2 (`message_server.yml` per-instance, containing "the Ed25519 attestation signing key"), Â§9.3 ("each entry signed by that server's own key") vs Spec C Â§7.6 and MASTER Â§9.4

location: Spec A Â§12.1 S8/S9 and Â§5.7 vs Spec B Â§4.3.1 (`HelloResponse.server_nonce`), Â§5.1 check 2, and Spec C Â§9.4 (bounded outbox)

location: Â§9.4 Key-transparency log (operator side), Â§9.5
problem:

location: Â§9.1 (Discovery / `server_signing_pub`), Â§4.3.1 `HelloResponse`, Â§10.2 (`message_server.yml`), Â§12.2 C-9

location: Â§11.2 enforcement item 1 (decision B11 / `redact/` package), Â§3.1, Â§13

location: Spec B Â§8.2 (grant token) and Â§4.1 (bulk plane)

location: Spec B decision B3 and Â§2.4 vs Â§7.2 (EPH(0) row) and Â§4.3.5 (TransientPush)

Â§7.2 says EPH(0) is 'never persisted; fanned out through Redis to online subscribers and dropped', but B3 and Â§2.4 state that no record ciphertext ever crosses Redis and fix the pub/sub payload as exactly `{mask, group_id_enc, lo_record_id, hi_record_id}` â€” a record-id range whose entire mechanism is 'the receiving instance re-reads Postgres'. For EPH(0) there is nothing in Postgres to re-read. With the required N â‰¥ 2 replicas, read receipts and typing indicators â€” both ON by default per MASTER Â§12.2 â€” reach only the subscribers who happen to have landed on the same instance as the sender. Add a second channel `urmsg:t:<mask>` whose payload is `AEAD(channel_key, transient_record_bytes)`, with Â§2.4's existing deployment requirements (no AOF/RDB, MONITOR denied by ACL, slowlog off) named as the compensating control and the carve-out bounded to records that by construction never touch disk. Then specify the EPH(0) submit path in Â§6: checks 1â€“8 of Â§5.1 apply, no transaction is opened, no `record_id` is allocated, `message_sender` is not updated, and `SubmitResult.record_id` is 0.

location: Spec B Â§4.3.3 (`Record`), Â§4.3.4 (FetchResponse), Â§4.3.5 (RecordPush), Â§4.4
problem: The `Record` message has no `record_id` field. MASTER Â§8 lists `record_id` as part of the RECORD ('server-assigned AFTER acceptance; pagination only; never authenticated'), and B's whole hole-detection and resume story depends on the client seeing ids, but `FetchResponse.records` and `RecordPush.records` carry only bodies. `RecordPush` has no base id at all â€” only `high_water_record_id` â€” so its 'always contiguous in record_id' claim has nothing to anchor to, and Â§4.4 step 4's 'discard every buffered record with record_id <= snapshot_record_id' is not executable on the client side either. location: Spec B Â§4.3.4 (attestation signature input)
problem: The attestation signature does not cover the fetch filter, so a filtered fetch cannot serve as the evidence C-4 requires. The preimage is `since â€– until â€– high_water â€– count â€– record_ids â€– server_time` with no `class_mask` and no `heads_only`. An attestation over a `class_mask = PERMANENT` fetch is byte-indistinguishable from an attestation over an unfiltered range that omitted every other record â€” which is exactly the withholding signature C-4 tells the client to act on ('warn when a later-learned record falls inside a covering attestation that omitted it'). Every filtered fetch therefore either raises a false alarm or gives a dishonest server a free way to launder a withheld record.
fix: Append `â€– u32(class_mask) â€– u8(heads_only)` to the Â§4.3.4 signature input and add both fields to `FetchAttestation`. Have C-4 compare attestations only within an identical filter. If that is judged too subtle for the client, refuse to attest any fetch with `class_mask != 0` and return the attestation field empty.

location: Spec B Â§4.3.1 (Capabilities defaults) and Â§4.6
problem: `max_records_per_submit` and `max_request_bytes` are mutually inconsistent, so a client obeying the advertised contract can build a request the server must reject. The advertised defaults are 64 records per submit, a top inline size bucket of 65536 bytes, and (Â§4.6) a working `max_request_bytes` of 131072. Sixty-four records at the top bucket is ~4 MiB â€” thirty-two times the reassembly cap â€” and Â§5.1 check 1 rejects it with REASON_OVERSIZE only after the client has fragmented and sent every byte. There is no statement anywhere that both caps bind.

Better: replace `max_records_per_submit` with `max_submit_bytes` and let the client pack to the byte budget, which is the constraint that actually matters and removes the inconsistency by construction. Propagate the rule to Â§12.2 as a new C-item, since Spec C's send queue is what will build the oversized batch.

location: Spec B Â§6.1 step 1 and Â§4.3.3 (SubmitResponse)
problem: Batch atomicity versus gapless `record_id` is unspecified, and the two plausible readings differ. Step (1) allocates a block of `$n` ids up front, but `SubmitResponse` returns a positional `SubmitResult` per record, implying partial acceptance. If some records in a batch are rejected inside the transaction (stream-index regression, idempotent retry, blob incomplete) while others commit, the allocated block exceeds the rows written and the group's `record_id` sequence acquires a permanent gap â€” destroying the property decision B4 exists to create and that C-4 instructs clients to treat as a fault.
fix: Make the batch all-or-nothing and say so in Â§6.1. Run every per-record check â€” including the hoisted idempotency probe â€” before allocation; compute the exact accepted count `k`; allocate `k` in step (1); insert. Any rejection that surfaces inside the transaction rolls the whole batch back, and every `SubmitResult` carries a reason with zero rows written. Add it to Â§13 as a test: a 5-record batch whose third record regresses its stream index leaves `next_record_id` unchanged.

location: Spec B Â§3.2 migration 001 (`next_record_id DEFAULT 0`) vs Â§4.3.4 (`since_record_id` exclusive)
problem: `next_record_id` defaults to 0 while `since_record_id` is documented as exclusive, so a fresh client can never fetch `record_id = 0` â€” which under Â§4.3.2 is the group's initial commit, the record from which all epoch state derives. `uint64` has no value below 0 to pass as an exclusive lower bound, so the first record of every group is permanently unfetchable by any client that did not create it.

Cheaper and less error-prone than redefining `since_record_id` as inclusive, which would change every caller and every cursor already described in Â§4.4 and Â§12.2 C-7.

location: Spec A Â§12.1 S2 vs Spec B Â§3.2 migration 004 (`message_record_stream`) and migration 005, vs MASTER Â§8
problem: Three documents disagree on the uniqueness domain of `stream_index`. MASTER Â§8 says 'monotonic per (`sender_handle`)'. Spec A's S2 requires the server to enforce monotonicity 'per `(group_id, sender_handle, retention_class)`'. If the client follows A and keeps one counter per class, its first EPH record and its first DURABLE record both carry index 0, and B rejects the second as REASON_STREAM_INDEX_REUSED. This is the write path â€” it fails on the first message of the first conversation, and the failure is a per-class off-by-one that a single-class functional test will not reach.

Recommend MASTER's per-`sender_handle` domain: a single counter is what makes MASTER Â§8's durable 'index k consumed' record one fsync per record rather than one per class, and it keeps B's index and `message_sender` as written. Strike `retention_class` from A's S2. Add a case to the shared interop vector file (A-8): two records at the same index in different classes, expected verdict REASON_STREAM_INDEX_REUSED.

location: MASTER Â§9.2, Spec A Â§12.1 ('What we give the server') vs Spec B Â§5.3 and decision B9
problem: Three documents disagree on whether the server holds `write_key`, and the two that are wrong are the two the implementer reads first. location: Spec B Â§4.3.1 (HelloResponse.server_nonce, Capabilities) and Â§5.1 check 2, vs Spec A Â§12.1 S8/S9
problem: `server_nonce` rotation is required by Spec A and absent from Spec B. location: Spec B Â§5.1 check 5 (known-group filter) and Â§2.4 (`urmsg:gf:epoch`)

location: Spec B Â§3.2 migration 001 (`blob_quota_bytes`)

location: Spec B Â§4.3.3 (`expire_at_ms`), Â§5.4 (amended preimage), Â§3.2 migration 003 (`expire_at timestamp`)
problem: `expire_at` has three representations and no stated conversion: `expire_at_ms` on the wire, `u64(expire_at)` in the `write_auth` preimage and `AAD_head`, and `timestamp` in the DDL. location: Spec B decision B2 vs Â§4.7 (Redis unavailability)
problem: B2 states that 'no correctness invariant may depend on [Redis] ... Losing Redis degrades latency and push liveness; it never changes what is accepted or stored.' Â§4.7 then states that on Redis unavailability all limits fail closed to an in-process limiter at 25% of the configured rate â€” which is precisely a change in what is accepted. location: Spec B Â§5.1 check 8 and Â§8.3 (assembly, binding)
problem: `body_hash` is never verified for blob-backed records. Check 8 applies only 'for inline bodies', and Â§8.3's binding step checks only `state == COMPLETE`. The server already streams every byte during assembly, so hashing is free, and without it a bad or truncated blob is discovered only by a recipient after downloading up to 100 MB over the mesh.

location: Spec B Â§4.3.1 (server_signing_pub, BlobEndpoint.tls_spki_sha256), Â§9.1, Â§12.2 C-9
